record.original_question: Does every non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?

evidence.quote: Question 43. — Does any non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A compact complex surface $X$ is called non-Kähler if it does not admit any Kähler metric; equivalently, its first Betti number is odd. A birational structure on a complex manifold $X$ is a maximal atlas of local biholomorphisms from open subsets of $X$ to open subsets of a fixed compact complex surface $S$ (for instance $\mathbb{P}^2$) whose transition maps are restrictions of birational self-maps of $S$. Equivalently, it is given by a developing map from the universal cover of $X$ to $S$ that is equivariant under a holonomy representation of $\pi_1(X)$ into the group $\mathrm{Bir}(S)$ of birational self-maps of $S$, with the developing map being a local biholomorphism.

Question: Does every non-Kähler compact complex surface admit a birational structure?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in the literature as a conjecture, with partial results: Hopf surfaces and certain Kato surfaces (e.g. those with a cycle and one branch of rational curves) are known to admit special birational structures, but the general case for arbitrary non-Kähler compact complex surfaces (including Inoue surfaces and general Kato surfaces) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Special birational structures on non-Kählerian complex surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Kato surfaces with a cycle and only one branch of rational curves admit a special birational structure; conjecture that all compact non-Kählerian complex surfaces admit birational structures.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as a conjecture with only partial results established.
